content.title: WHAT DOCTORS DO {{RIGHT BEFORE BED}} THAT YOU'D NEVER GUESS
facts: **Fruit juice instead of whole fruit** -> spikes blood sugar faster than a candy bar because the fiber that slows absorption is gone.
**Sleeping in on weekends** -> shifts your internal clock like mini jet lag, making Monday mornings harder.
**Wearing sunglasses all day, even when it's mild out** -> can confuse your body's light-based wake-up signal if overused.
**Taking a hot shower right before bed** -> feels relaxing but can delay sleep onset if it's too close to lights-out, since your core temp needs to drop first.
**Snacking on almonds straight from a big bag** -> a 'healthy' fat can turn into a calorie surplus fast without noticing portions.
**Using mouthwash right after brushing** -> can rinse away the concentrated fluoride your toothpaste just left behind.
**Stretching cold muscles before a run** -> may loosen joints too much and slightly raise injury risk instead of preventing it.
**Cracking your knuckles out of habit** -> won't cause arthritis, but repeated force over years can slightly loosen the joint capsule.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
Let's talk about a few of these. Fruit juice loses almost all its fiber during processing, so the natural sugars hit your bloodstream in one quick wave instead of a slow release, which is why juice can spike blood sugar more than people expect. Mouthwash right after brushing might feel extra clean, but it washes away the concentrated fluoride layer your toothpaste just deposited, so it actually works better used at a different time of day. And that hot pre-bed shower isn't bad, timing just matters: your body needs a slight core temperature drop to trigger sleepiness, so showering too close to bedtime can briefly delay that signal. Everyone's routine is different, so notice what actually changes how you feel.
